properties.natural_language: Before processing any JSON-RPC state query, the block parameter MUST be validated: if object format, blockNumber and blockHash MUST NOT both be present simultaneously.

Before executing a state query, the JSON-RPC block parameter format MUST be correctly detected as one of: hex string (QUANTITY), tag string (earliest/latest/pending/safe/finalized), or object with blockNumber/blockHash fields.
Before a JSON-RPC state query is processed, the client-supplied block parameter MUST be parseable into a valid block identifier; malformed parameters MUST result in a JSON-RPC error response.
When a block parameter object contains both blockNumber and blockHash fields, the request MUST always be rejected as invalid, regardless of whether the values are consistent.
If an object-format block parameter contains neither blockNumber nor blockHash, the request MUST be treated as invalid.
The requireCanonical field MUST have no effect when the block parameter is the 'pending' tag, since pending state is inherently non-canonical.
After looking up a block by hash that does not exist in the database, the system MUST return JSON-RPC error code -32001.
After checking canonical status when requireCanonical=true and the block is not on the canonical chain, the system MUST return JSON-RPC error code -32000.
After a state query executes successfully at a canonical block, the result MUST be returned to the client with no error.
The node MUST have access to historical state data for the requested block; if state has been pruned, the query MUST fail gracefully rather than returning incorrect data.
A block hash MUST uniquely identify a single block and its associated state across all forks known to the node.
The node's canonical chain determination MUST be consistent and trustworthy; a compromised canonical status could mislead clients into trusting non-canonical state.
After detecting a block parameter in object format, the validation step MUST verify mutual exclusivity of blockNumber and blockHash before proceeding to block lookup.
Before accepting an eth/69 peer status message, the receiving node MUST validate that networkid, genesis hash, and forkid match its own values; incompatible peers MUST be disconnected.
Before trusting a peer's earliestBlock and latestBlock claims from eth/69 status, the node MUST treat these values as unverified self-reports until confirmed by actual block requests.
Before accepting a BlockRangeUpdate (0x11) message, the node MUST verify that no more than one such update has been received from the same peer within the current epoch (32 blocks).
Before using receipt data received via eth/69 GetReceipts, the receiving node MUST recompute bloom filters from the log data, since eth/69 receipts omit bloom filters.
Peers that claim to serve a block range but fail to provide blocks within that range MUST be penalized via peer scoring.
The eth/69 receipt format [tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, logs] MUST be correctly parsed; any malformed receipt data MUST be rejected.
Sufficient nodes on the network MUST continue serving historical data to ensure new nodes can sync; history expiry MUST NOT prevent block availability for post-merge blocks.
After successfully validating a peer's status in eth/69 handshake, the connection MUST be established and the peer's history range stored locally.
After receiving a BlockRangeUpdate message, the peer's known history range MUST be updated in the local peer table.
After recomputing bloom filters from eth/69 receipt logs, the receipts MUST be functionally equivalent to full receipts for local query purposes.
The network MUST have migrated away from total difficulty reliance post-merge; removing TD from the eth/69 handshake MUST NOT break compatibility with active peers.
Before accepting an eth/70 peer status, the receiving node MUST validate networkid, genesis, and forkid; the blockRange field MUST be stored but treated as unverified.

Before relying on a SendBlockRange (0x0c) response, the node MUST treat the reported ranges as unverified claims; dishonest claims detected via failed block requests MUST trigger peer scoring penalties.
Before processing multiple [startBlock, endBlock] tuples from a SendBlockRange response, the node MUST union them to determine total peer availability for non-contiguous ranges.
Peer range advertisements MUST be verified through actual block requests before being fully trusted; the system MUST NOT make sync decisions solely based on unverified range claims.
The peer selection mechanism MUST maintain diverse peer connections to resist Sybil attacks; the system MUST NOT allow coordinated false range advertisements to monopolize peer slots.
After a peer fails to provide blocks within its advertised range, the peer MUST be flagged as unreliable and its peer score decreased.
After completing eth/70 handshake, the peer's block range MUST be stored and available for peer selection decisions.
When disconnecting a peer to make room for a range-providing peer, the disconnection exception MUST only be applied when no existing connected peer covers the needed block range.
Nodes MUST maintain accurate knowledge of their own block availability; honest nodes MUST NOT inadvertently advertise incorrect ranges.
Historical block storage solutions (per EIP-4444) MUST be deployed before wide-scale block range pruning occurs to prevent permanent data loss.
The gas cost for KECCAK256 MUST always equal GAS_KECCAK256 (30) + GAS_KECCAK256_WORD (6) * ceil(size/32) + memory_expansion_cost; no execution path may bypass gas charging.
Word count calculation for KECCAK256 gas MUST use ceiling division: words = ceil(size / 32). A size of 0 MUST result in 0 words.
The Keccak-256 hash implementation MUST be cryptographically secure; hash output MUST be deterministic for identical inputs across all implementations.
Memory expansion gas cost MUST grow quadratically to prevent memory exhaustion attacks; the cost formula MUST make large memory allocations prohibitively expensive.
After KECCAK256 execution completes, exactly one 32-byte hash value MUST have been pushed onto the stack and the program counter MUST have been incremented by 1.
After gas deduction, if gas_left is insufficient, an OutOfGasError MUST be raised and execution MUST revert.
Before KECCAK256 execution, there MUST be at least 2 elements on the stack (memory_start_index and size); if fewer than 2, a StackUnderflowError MUST be raised.
After memory expansion, the memory MUST be zero-padded to the new size rounded to 32-byte word boundaries.
Memory read operations MUST only access the EVM's internal memory space; out-of-bounds reads beyond the expanded memory MUST NOT occur.
After comparing memory bounds, if the requested range exceeds current memory size, the expansion path MUST be taken; otherwise, the direct read path MUST be used.
Before propagating a beacon block received via gossip, the block MUST pass all consensus-layer validation (slot, proposer, signature, parent) and execution payload timestamp check.

Before downscoring a peer for an invalid block, the node MUST distinguish between consensus-layer invalidity and execution-layer-only invalidity; blocks failing only execution validation MUST NOT trigger peer downscoring.
Before responding to a BeaconBlocksByRange/v2 or BeaconBlocksByRoot/v2 request, the responder MUST determine the correct fork version for each requested block slot to use the appropriate SSZ schema.
The maximum message size for beacon block gossip and req/resp chunks MUST be 10 MiB; any message exceeding this limit MUST be rejected at the network layer.
Optimistic and non-optimistic nodes MUST receive and propagate the same blocks on the gossip network to prevent network segregation.
Only the legitimate block proposer for a given slot can create blocks that pass consensus validation; an attacker MUST NOT be able to cheaply generate invalid-execution blocks at scale.
After a block fails consensus-layer validation, it MUST be rejected and MUST NOT be propagated to peers.
After a block passes consensus validation, it MUST be propagated to peers even before execution payload verification completes.
After serializing a block response, each chunk MUST use the fork-version-appropriate SSZ schema (phase0, altair, or bellatrix) determined by the block's slot.
Tracing MUST be disabled by default via the discard_evm_trace no-op tracer; tracing MUST only be active when explicitly enabled by a debugging tool.
Custom tracer implementations MUST NOT interfere with EVM execution; the tracer callback MUST be purely observational and MUST NOT modify EVM state.
Tracer callbacks MUST execute quickly and MUST NOT significantly impact EVM execution time; slow tracers could delay transaction processing.
Trace data exposed to external tracers MUST follow EIP-3155 format standards for compatibility with debugging and analysis tools.
Before a trace event can be captured, the module does not implement trace collection itself; implementers MUST provide storage, formatting, or transmission capabilities.
The EvmTracer Protocol's __call__ parameter 'evm: object' MUST refer to the live EVM execution context, providing access to stack, memory, PC, and gas state.
After setting a custom tracer via set_evm_trace, the previous tracer MUST be returned to the caller to enable proper restoration.
After a transaction completes, a TransactionEnd event MUST be emitted with gas consumed, output data, and optional error information.
After an opcode throws an exception, an OpException event MUST be emitted and the exception MUST be recorded by the tracer.
After restoring a previous tracer, the restored tracer MUST become the active receiver of all subsequent trace events.
Sensitive EVM state data (stack, memory, storage) exposed through trace events MAY be logged, stored, or transmitted by the tracer; operators MUST be aware of the data leakage risk.
The upgrade cadence MUST be a multiple of 3 months (3, 6, 9, or 12 months); cadences of 4 or 5 months MUST be rejected.
Consecutive quarterly roadmap windows MUST NOT be used for upgrades; there MUST be at least one unused window between consecutive roadmap upgrades.
Critical upgrades addressing systemic risk MUST be deployable immediately without scheduling constraints; they MUST NOT be delayed by the cadence framework.
After selecting a roadmap window, the upgrade activation MUST have at least 4-6 weeks of lead time before the target Wednesday 12:00 UTC.
After applying block number conventions, mainnet activation blocks MUST end with 000 or more zeros, and testnet activation blocks MUST be palindromic numbers.
Block times MUST be predictable enough to estimate activation block numbers weeks in advance; significant variance could cause activation outside the target window.
Node operators MUST have sufficient time (2-6 weeks) to update their software before activation; insufficient lead time could cause chain splits.
The core development community MUST adhere to this scheduling framework consistently; deviation could harm ecosystem stability.
After classifying an upgrade as Roadmap, the scheduling MUST use one of the four quarterly windows (third Wednesday of Jan, Apr, Jul, or Oct).
After classifying an upgrade as Priority, the scheduling MUST use any unused roadmap window with 2-4 weeks lead time.
The term 'production grade networks' MUST refer to mainnet and any testnet with significant economic value or user base.
Gas charging MUST always check sufficiency before deduction; if gas_left < required gas, an OutOfGasError MUST be raised before any state modification.
After successful gas charging, evm.gas_left MUST be reduced by exactly the charged amount.
Memory expansion gas cost MUST follow the formula (size_in_words * 3) + (size_in_words^2 / 512); the quadratic component MUST prevent unbounded memory allocation.
Arithmetic operations for gas calculations MUST NOT overflow within uint256 bounds; overflow could lead to incorrect gas charging or free execution.
Gas refunds MUST be bounded (capped at a percentage of total gas used) to prevent gas token exploitation.
Cold storage access (first access) MUST charge 2100 gas; subsequent warm accesses to the same slot MUST charge only 100 gas.
Setting storage from zero to non-zero MUST cost 20000 gas; updating non-zero to non-zero MUST cost 5000 gas; clearing to zero MUST yield a 4800 gas refund.
The blob base fee MUST be calculated using an exponential formula based on excess blob gas from the parent block; the minimum blob gas price MUST be enforced.
After calculating blob data fee, the total fee MUST equal (blob_count * GAS_PER_BLOB) * blob_base_fee.
The 63/64 rule MUST be applied for all message calls: maximum gas forwarded to subcall = gas_left - (gas_left / 64), ensuring parent retains 1/64 for cleanup.
After gas allocation for a value-transferring CALL, a 2300 gas stipend MUST be added to the subcall's gas allocation.
After memory extension, the EVM memory size MUST be rounded up to the nearest 32-byte word boundary.
BLS precompile gas MUST be charged upfront before execution, following the same pattern as other precompiles.
After charging base call cost, if value > 0, an additional 9000 gas MUST be charged; if the target is a new account, an additional 25000 gas MUST be charged.
Before accepting a block into fork choice, the block MUST have passed parent validation (parent exists in store), slot validation, and finality constraint checks in sequence.
Before confirming data availability, all column sidecars MUST be structurally verified via verify_data_column_sidecar AND cryptographically verified via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs.
Before executing state transition, is_data_available MUST be called with hash_tree_root(block) WITHOUT passing blob_kzg_commitments, relying on DAS-based verification instead.
Data availability MUST only be guaranteed within the MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS window; column sidecars beyond this window MAY be unavailable.
The KZG commitment scheme used for column sidecar verification MUST be cryptographically sound; forging valid-looking sidecars for unavailable data MUST be computationally infeasible.
An attacker MUST NOT be able to selectively withhold specific columns while making others available in a way that prevents reconstruction of the complete data.
After data availability check fails, the block MAY be queued for later processing rather than permanently rejected.
After successful state transition, the block MUST be stored in the fork choice store and considered for head selection.
After KZG proof verification fails for any column sidecar, the data MUST be marked as unavailable for that block.
Column sidecar retrieval is implementation-dependent; implementations MAY use any combination of local storage, P2P requests, and DAS sampling.
The referenced execution-specs and consensus-specs repositories MUST contain correct and complete specifications; implementations MUST treat referenced versions as authoritative.
EIP-7568 MUST serve as the canonical cross-reference point for network upgrade specifications; conflicts between referenced spec versions indicate implementation bugs.
De-duplication means providing canonical pointers to authoritative spec sources, not removing existing specification text from other repositories.
The timestamp-based activation mechanism MUST correctly coordinate simultaneous EL and CL upgrades; timing mismatch could cause chain splits.
After activation timestamp is reached, both EL (Shanghai) and CL (Capella) rules MUST be activated simultaneously; neither layer may activate independently.
Developers and implementers MUST use EIP-7568 as the authoritative reference for finding upgrade specifications to prevent implementation divergence.
After resolving Shapella upgrade references, the system MUST identify it as the first coordinated EL+CL upgrade using timestamp-based activation.
